key_insight: CQMOM captures coupled size, shape, and velocity distributions of oblate spheroidal particles at over 60 times lower computational cost than a single Monte Carlo realization.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports efficient modeling of non-spherical particle transport, breakage, and classification while preserving geometric–kinematic correlations.
method: Represent size, aspect ratio, and three velocity components using conditional quadrature.
Assume particles continuously adopt their drag-maximizing orientation.
Apply Strang splitting to continuous and discontinuous moment-transport operators.
evidence_signal: Against Monte Carlo tests covering drag, breakage, recoil, and attrition at different Stokes numbers, two nodes per coordinate reproduced particle number and mean geometry within statistical uncertainty, with velocity statistics agreeing to within 7%.
watch_item: Conditional velocity quadrature is the main source of residual error, and the drag-maximizing orientation assumption restricts the modeled orientation dynamics.
paper_title: A conditional quadrature method of moments for populations of oblate spheroidal particles
